newsitem.title: UK: IATA sees $4.4 billion airline profit in 1997.
newsitem.headline: IATA sees $4.4 billion airline profit in 1997.

text.p: Airlines are on course for a collective before-tax profit of $4.4 billion in 1997 on scheduled international services against $4.0 billion last year, the Internationational Air Transport Association(IATA) said.

The current forecast is based on all available information and is the mid-range for estimates ranging from a high of $7.2 billion to a low of $2.1 billion, IATA director of aviation information, Peter Morris told a news conference.
The comparative figure for 1995 was $5.1 billion.
Separately IATA director general, Pierre Jeanniot said that traffic and capacity look set to increase by around seven percent and 7.5 percent respectively in 1997.
Last year traffic and capacity rose by 8.4 percent and 7.9 percent, while average yields fells by 2.5 percent with unit costs decreasing at a slower rate of one percent.

However "if improvements are to be seen in overall airline financial results, continued efforts cost containment coupled with increase in yields will be necessary," Jeanniot wrote in a foreword to IATA latest World Air Transport Statistics.
"Attention should also be paid to gearing any fleet expansion to expected levels of long term profitability.
